title: A1: Survive and be understood in Canada
outcome: Understand and say basic things in real Canadian situations, and answer the first (easiest) items of a TCF listening and reading test. TCF scale for this band: listening/reading 100 to 199.

unit_template.title: New words (1 of 2)
unit_template.note: exactly 5 words with sound, meaning, example

unit_template.title: New words (2 of 2)
unit_template.note: exactly 5 words with sound, meaning, example

unit_template.title: One rule
unit_template.note: plain English first, then French examples and drills

unit_template.title: Hear it, read it
unit_template.note: short Canadian scene using only taught words

unit_template.title: TCF corner and checkpoint
unit_template.note: exam-format items from this unit only, then 10-question checkpoint

units.title: Introduce yourself
units.situation: Meeting a neighbour, a coworker or a clinic receptionist for the first time.
units.can_do: Say my name, where I am from, what languages I speak, and greet people politely.
units.canada_context: Allô and bonjour, tu vs vous with a stranger or an official, introducing yourself at an immigration or clinic desk.
canada_vs_france: allô is a normal greeting in Canada
bonjour is also used as goodbye in Québec

units.title: Greet, be polite, spell your name
units.situation: Starting a phone call, spelling a name and an email, thanking someone.
units.can_do: Greet at different times of day, be polite, ask someone to repeat or spell, and spell my own name and email.
units.canada_context: Spelling a name to Service Canada or a landlord, giving a courriel, answering the phone.
canada_vs_france: bienvenue means you're welcome in Canada
courriel is the Canadian word for email

tcf_corner.speaking: Task 1 style: spell and give details

units.title: Forms and papers
units.situation: Filling in a form at a clinic, bank or government office.
units.can_do: Understand and fill basic personal details on a form and say them aloud.
units.canada_context: NAS (numéro d'assurance sociale), health card, postal code, province, permanent resident paperwork.
canada_vs_france: code postal format (A1A 1A1)
province vs département

tcf_corner.listening: an agent reading details back, 4 options

units.title: Family and people
units.situation: Showing photos and talking about family at work or with a neighbour.
units.can_do: Name family members, say whose something is, and describe a person simply.
units.canada_context: conjoint(e) and enfants on official forms, family sponsorship vocabulary at a basic level.
canada_vs_france: conjoint(e) is the official term for spouse or partner in Canada

tcf_corner.reading: a short message about a family

units.title: Numbers, money and prices
units.situation: Paying at a store, reading a price, understanding rent or a bill.
units.can_do: Understand and say numbers and prices in dollars, and read simple prices.
units.canada_context: Dollars, cents, TPS/TVQ style taxes at a basic level, tipping, rabais and soldes.
canada_vs_france: dollars and cents, not euros
taxes are added at the register

tcf_corner.writing: guided: short message about a price

units.title: Days, time and appointments
units.situation: Booking and confirming an appointment, reading a schedule.
units.can_do: Say and understand days, dates and clock times, and arrange a simple appointment.
units.canada_context: Clinic appointments, bus schedules, office hours, written time like 9 h 30.
canada_vs_france: Canadian written time uses h (9 h 30)
24 hour and 12 hour usage

units.title: Eating: déjeuner, dîner, souper
units.situation: Ordering at a restaurant and talking about meals.
units.can_do: Name common foods and meals, order, and say what I like.
units.canada_context: Restaurant ordering, tipping, meal words and times as used in Canada.
canada_vs_france: Canada: déjeuner = breakfast, dîner = lunch, souper = dinner
France: petit-déjeuner, déjeuner, dîner

tcf_corner.writing: guided: a short note about a meal

units.title: Groceries and shopping
units.can_do: Ask for items and quantities, understand a store notice, and say what is missing.
units.canada_context: Dépanneur, épicerie, supermarché, pharmacie, bags and receipts.
canada_vs_france: dépanneur (corner store) is a Québec word
magasiner means to shop in Canada

tcf_corner.reading: a shopping list and a notice

units.title: Getting around
units.situation: Asking directions, using the bus and metro, travelling in a city.
units.can_do: Ask and understand simple directions, buy a ticket, and say where I am going.
units.canada_context: Autobus, métro, arrêt, stationnement, street signs, ride schedules.
canada_vs_france: autobus and stationnement in Canada vs bus and parking
Canadian road signs

tcf_corner.writing: guided: explain how to get somewhere

units.title: Housing and the lease
units.situation: Looking at an apartment, talking to a landlord.
units.can_do: Describe a home, understand a rental ad, and ask basic questions about an apartment.
units.canada_context: Appartement, bail, loyer, propriétaire, locataire, Québec apartment notation like 3 1/2.
canada_vs_france: bail and loyer, with 3 1/2 style counting in Québec
logement vs appartement

tcf_corner.speaking: Task 1 style: ask about an apartment
tcf_corner.writing: guided: a short message to a landlord

units.title: Weather and clothes
units.situation: Talking about the weather and what to wear in a Canadian winter.
units.can_do: Understand a simple forecast, say what the weather is, and choose clothes.
units.canada_context: Winter weather, snow, cold, forecast words, temperatures in degrees Celsius.
canada_vs_france: tuque is a Canadian word for a winter hat
Celsius, with very low winter temperatures

tcf_corner.speaking: Task 1 style: talk about the weather

units.title: Work and studies
units.situation: Talking about your job, your studies and your workday.
units.can_do: Say what job or studies I have, describe a simple workday, and ask a coworker simple questions.
units.canada_context: Entrevue (interview), CV, employer, schedule, university and cégep recognition.
canada_vs_france: entrevue in Canada vs entretien
cégep is Québec only

tcf_corner.listening: a coworker talking about work, 4 options
tcf_corner.speaking: Task 1 style: talk about my work

units.title: Health and services
units.situation: Describing a problem at a pharmacy or walk-in clinic and calling for help.
units.can_do: Name body parts, say what hurts, understand basic instructions, and call for help.
units.canada_context: Clinique sans rendez-vous, pharmacie, urgence, ordonnance, médecin de famille, 911.
canada_vs_france: clinique sans rendez-vous (walk-in clinic)
health card instead of the French carte vitale

tcf_corner.speaking: Task 1 style: describe a health problem
tcf_corner.writing: guided: a short message to a clinic

units.title: Free time and simple plans
units.situation: Inviting a friend, talking about weekends and plans.
units.can_do: Say what I like to do, invite someone, accept or refuse, and say what I will do this weekend.
units.canada_context: Fin de semaine plans, hockey and winter sports, invitations, community events.
canada_vs_france: fin de semaine is common in Canada, week-end in France

mini_mocks.note: one-play listening, 4 options, answers hidden until the end
adds Canadian accents (Camille, Mathieu) to the listening
ends with estimated A1 level and what to fix
